subtitle: Nasdaq: CAI  -  molecular diagnostics / tumor profiling  -  IPO diligence, updated to current filings (as of 2026-05-29)
verdict: Disclosure-honest IPO whose headline bad fact has since closed. The prospectus carried an auditor-attested going-concern, but the offering did exactly what it was structured to do: as of the FY2025 10-K and Q1-2026 10-Q the going-concern is gone, the term loan is repaid, the notes and preferred have converted, and the company holds ~$820M cash. No fabricated claims were found. The remaining live flags are governance, not solvency: concentrated founder control (Halbert 43.9%) and a founder share-pledge that has GROWN to 25M+ shares post-IPO, plus one marketing-vs-registry patent-count overstatement.
recommendation: RECOMMENDATION -- CONSTRUCTIVE, position-sized to governance/insider supply. This review tests two things and they now point the same way. (1) Disclosure honesty (the credibility axis): Caris stated its hard facts plainly and the post-IPO record confirms them -- zero fabricated claims, and the headline going-concern resolved exactly as the offering was structured to resolve it. (2) Operating trajectory (the fundamentals axis, added this revision): the XBRL actuals show a business inflecting, not deteriorating -- revenue compounding +79% to +113% YoY (Q1'25 $121M -> Q1'26 $216M), operating margin climbing from -67% (Q2'24) toward breakeven (+2% in Q1'26), ~$820M cash at 2026-03-31, and a guidance record that is conservative-and-beaten: FY2025 was guided up from $0.68-0.69B to $0.72-0.73B and then ACTUALLY landed ~$812M (an ~11% beat), and FY2026 was issued at $1.0-1.02B and reaffirmed at Q1. Put together, the ~60% drawdown from the $42.50 peak to ~$17 is a float/dilution/valuation unwind of a tiny-float IPO pop, NOT a fundamental or disclosure failure -- the numbers an honest issuer would have to hide are absent. CAVEAT on the read: the strongest single quarter, derived Q4'25 (+30% operating margin, $82M net income, $293M revenue), is computed as the FY2025 10-K minus the first three 10-Qs and is visibly lumpy versus the quarters around it; treat it as carrying annual true-ups (year-end revenue recognition, reserve releases) rather than as a sustainable run-rate, and anchor the trajectory to the smoother Q1'26 (+2% operating margin) instead. WHAT REMAINS LIVE is therefore not credibility and not solvency but governance/insider supply: a founder controlling 43.9% in a single share class, a 25M-share founder pledge (~8.8% of shares outstanding) that is a standing margin-call channel, and ongoing post-lock-up insider distribution (Form 144/Form 4) against a ~283M-share base. Net: a disclosure-honest issuer with a genuinely improving P&L whose risk is ownership structure, not the business -- size any position to the governance/insider-supply profile, not to a liquidity cliff (which no longer exists) or a growth scare (which the actuals do not support).
exec_summary: Scope and time-awareness. This is an IPO-disclosure diligence of Caris's final priced prospectus (Form 424B4, effective 2025-06-20) UPDATED to the current filing record as of 2026-05-29. Where the prospectus made a forward-looking or solvency claim, we did not stop at the prospectus -- we read the post-IPO filings the claim pointed to: the FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-03), three post-IPO Form 10-Qs (the latest filed 2026-05-08), the 2026 proxy (DEF 14A, filed 2026-04-23), and the post-lock-up insider record (Form 144 / Form 4). We declared eleven issuer characteristics and tested twelve high-discrimination claims against independent authorities -- external registries (ClinicalTrials.gov, USPTO Open Data Portal, openFDA, SEC EDGAR) plus structural reads of the filings themselves. Net result across the twelve claims: zero hard negatives, four moderate flags, five corroborated, three honestly unverifiable.

Headline -- the going concern has CLOSED (verified). The prospectus disclosed a real FY2024 going-concern (Deloitte: 'substantial doubt'), and at IPO that was the dominant fundamental risk. The time-aware verdict reverses the severity: the FY2025 10-K audit opinion carries NO going-concern language; the IPO raised $519.5M net; cash stood at $819.9M at 2026-03-31 (versus $31.2M at Q1'2025); the 2023 Term Loan (~$381M carrying) was repaid in full on 2026-04-01; the 2025 Convertible Notes converted to common stock at the IPO; and the Series C/D/E/F redeemable preferred converted at the IPO, extinguishing the redemption rights. Deloitte was re-engaged and is up for ratification for FY2026. This is the model disclosure-honesty outcome: a hard bad fact disclosed candidly, then resolved exactly as the offering was structured to resolve it.

The one genuine claim-vs-registry divergence -- patent count. The prospectus claims '200+ patents granted (100+ pending).' USPTO Open Data Portal shows roughly 16-33 U.S.-granted patents for the Caris / Caris MPI assignees. The technology areas the company emphasizes (molecular profiling and digital-pathology AI/ML) are genuinely represented in the portfolio, so this is not an invented-capability claim; it reads as a family/jurisdiction/marketing-aggregate count rather than U.S. issued grants. Capped at moderate because the registry undercounts older and foreign-family grants -- but the 200+ figure is not supportable from the issued-patent record and should be read as a ceiling, not a fact.

Governance and insider supply (moderate, and the live risk now). Founder/Chairman/CEO David D. Halbert holds 43.9% of the ~282.7M shares outstanding (2026-03-31 proxy) in a single share class -- almost exactly the 44.6% the prospectus projected -- so public holders are a structural minority that cannot effect a change of control. The founder share-pledge has GROWN since the prospectus: 25,000,000 shares (Halbert Family Capital, LLC) are now pledged against personal debt -- ~8.8% of shares outstanding and ~20% of Halbert's holding -- a materially larger forced-sale channel than the 1.66M shares disclosed at IPO. The 180-day lock-up expired ~December 2025 and insider sale notices (Form 144 on 2025-12-11, Form 4s through 2026-05-18) confirm distribution is underway. None of this is a credibility flag; together it describes a founder-controlled issuer with ongoing insider supply.

Corroborated and honestly unverifiable. Corroborated: the FDA premarket approval (PMA) for MI Cancer Seek (November 2024) is concrete, dated, and uncontradicted; Caris's clinical evidence is registry/biorepository-based (five Caris-sponsored ClinicalTrials.gov studies including the POA Prospective Repository) exactly as the prospectus frames it, with no interventional-trial overclaim; emerging-growth-company status is accurate; and the pre-IPO auditor change (E&Y -> Deloitte) is now retired by two subsequent Deloitte audits and a FY2026 ratification vote. Unverifiable (no registry reaches them, scored without manufacturing severity): cumulative test volume (6.5M tests / 849k cases), the '100+ biopharma partners' roster (mega-pharma counterparties have no obligation to disclose a diagnostics vendor), and Medicare/MolDX coverage (CPT 0211U is a real proprietary-lab-analysis code, but coverage determinations are not a queryable federal registry).
appendix: Verification coverage and corpus. This review reads beyond the prospectus: the document corpus was refreshed to 2026-05-29 and includes the FY2025 Form 10-K (2026-03-03), three post-IPO Form 10-Qs (2025-08-12, 2025-11-05, 2026-05-08), eight Form 8-Ks, the 2026 proxy (DEF 14A, 2026-04-23), and the post-lock-up insider record. Fifteen knowledge-graph verification routines are applicable to a diagnostics IPO issuer of this profile. Nine were dispatched against specific claims (going-concern, auditor continuity, voting concentration, lock-up/overhang, related-party/pledge, JOBS-Act exemptions, underwriter profile, the ClinicalTrials.gov helper, and the patent search) and four were declined as not-applicable with reasons: no Up-C / tax-receivable-agreement structure (a Texas C-corp), no common-control combination, no pre-IPO debt-financed dividend recap, and federal-services revenue-concentration (the concentration axis here is payer/Medicare, not a federal contract). Two further routines -- an offshore ramp-and-dump archetype and Pentagon program-funding -- were marked applicable only by a keyword backstop firing on incidental filing mentions; neither is relevant to a founder-controlled Texas C-corp with no offshore domicile and no Department-of-Defense program revenue, and both were correctly excluded.

Method note. Claims (R) are taken from the issuer's priced prospectus; each is tested by an independent method f against an authority M. For solvency and time-sensitive claims, M is the post-IPO filing record (the FY2025 10-K, the Q1-2026 10-Q, the 2026 proxy, and EDGAR insider filings) rather than the prospectus's own forward-looking language -- this is what lets the review report that the disclosed going-concern has since closed rather than re-flagging a stale point-in-time risk. A finding of 'unverifiable' means no independent registry covers the claim -- it is neither corroboration nor contradiction, and is reported as such rather than converted into a severity score.
